cards.front: What is the general form of the full Fourier series for f(x) on [-π, π]?
State the three orthogonality integrals over [-π, π] for the set {1, cos(nx), sin(nx)}.
cards.back: ∫1·cos(nx) dx = 0, ∫1·sin(nx) dx = 0, ∫cos(nx)cos(mx) dx = π δ_{mn} (n,m≥1), ∫sin(nx)sin(mx) dx = π δ_{mn}, ∫cos(nx)sin(mx) dx = 0.

cards.front: Derive a_0 by integrating the Fourier series term-by-term over [-π, π].
cards.back: Integrate: ∫f(x) dx = ∫(a0/2) dx + 0 (all other terms integrate to zero by orthogonality). Thus a0 = (1/π) ∫_{-π}^π f(x) dx.

cards.front: Derive a_n (n≥1) by multiplying the series by cos(mx) and integrating.
cards.back: Multiply by cos(mx), integrate: left side gives ∫f cos(mx) dx. Right side: only a_m term survives, equaling a_m · π. Hence a_n = (1/π) ∫_{-π}^π f(x) cos(nx) dx.

cards.front: Derive b_n (n≥1) by multiplying the series by sin(mx) and integrating.
cards.back: Multiply by sin(mx), integrate: left side ∫f sin(mx) dx. Right side: only b_m term survives, equaling b_m · π. Hence b_n = (1/π) ∫_{-π}^π f(x) sin(nx) dx.

cards.front: Show how even/odd symmetry of f simplifies the coefficient formulas.
cards.back: If f even, bn=0 and an = (2/π)∫_0^π f(x)cos(nx)dx. If f odd, an=0 and bn = (2/π)∫_0^π f(x)sin(nx)dx.

cards.front: Starting from the inner-product definition, obtain all three coefficient formulas at once.
cards.back: The basis functions are orthogonal w.r.t. L2[-π,π] inner product ⟨g,h⟩=∫g h dx. Thus a0/2 = ⟨f,1⟩/⟨1,1⟩, an = ⟨f,cos(nx)⟩/⟨cos(nx),cos(nx)⟩, bn = ⟨f,sin(nx)⟩/⟨sin(nx),sin(nx)⟩, which recover the standard integral formulas.
